due_when.clears_when: the writer that holds trade_journal.db's write lock for >3 s during a burst is named from a measurement, and either fixed (no burst over a 48 h complete journalctl scan) or killed with a stated reason

origin.rerun: scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh 'journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live&since=<24h ago>&lines=200&grep=database%20is%20locked' (or the vm-diag-request relay with that path); count lines and bursts

what: Identify the holder of the trade_journal.db write lock behind the recurring 'database is locked' bursts on the live trader. MEASURED 2026-11-05 (journalctl via diag relay #23192/#23193, 2026-11-04T00:00Z to 2026-11-05T08:12Z): 59 lines in ~16 bursts of 10 s to 2 min; 55 are signal_audit_logger dual-write failures (a waiter, 3 s busy timeout), 4 are the 02:20Z order_monitor burst. The 08:00:30-08:01:12Z burst stretched an exit pass to 42.0 s and breached EXIT-EVAL INTERVAL (71.2 s). PR for TICK-STAGE2-RECONCILE-OFFTICK bounds the exit thread's exposure (0.25 s telemetry write timeout), but the holder is not known: the relay cannot see sqlite lock owners. Ruled out: ml_decision_shadow (no journal write), db_integrity (mode=ro). Next step: instrument write-transaction hold time in src.units.db.database.Database and the long-lived writers (thread + caller name when a commit follows >1 s after BEGIN), or sample /proc/<pid>/fd + journalctl at a burst via a system-action. | [2026-11-05 lane ML-ENTRY-WATCHDOG-EXIT] SECOND INSTANCE, MEASURED (journalctl via diag_fetch, 16:56:10-16:57:35Z, read_state complete, 463 lines): 'database is locked' on _sweep_package_close_reason_from_trade 16:56:49, venue_protection_snapshot 16:57:01, position_path_history 16:57:07, order_monitor protective-level sync + order_packages update 16:57:21/24, signal_audit_logger 16:57:29. The exit-loop's per-pass order_monitor lines gapped 16:56:15 -> 16:57:29 (74.0 s), which is the 16:58Z 'EXIT-EVAL INTERVAL BREACHED 74.3s' page (process started 16:51:10, so NOT the restart). Holder still unknown.
